title: Short A CVC Words — Write, Cut & Paste Activity (Adapting for Autism)

unmappedSkills.description: Read and write CVC words with short 'a' vowel sound (cab, mad, bag, ham, pan, map)

gaps: cut-and-paste-word-work: grid of CVC words with dotted-line cut strips at bottom, student writes the word then cuts and pastes a matching tile. Combines handwriting + tactile manipulation + reading in one activity.
leveled-word-work: same format but multiple difficulty tiers (Level 1 = 6 words, Level 2 = more words or blends, etc.) with a 'short [vowel]' header label

components.name: Write & Cut-Paste Grid
components.description: 6 CVC words with short 'a' (cab, mad, bag, ham, pan, map). Each word appears in a cell with: the printed word as reference, a writing line for the student to copy/write the word, and a cut-out tile at the bottom with the word to cut and paste. Labeled 'Level 1' — implies a progression system across the full product.
designPatterns: Multi-sensory reinforcement: see word → write word → cut tile → paste tile. Four modalities for one word.
Model-then-do: printed word is the model, writing line is the do
Tactile manipulation: physical cutting and pasting adds kinesthetic memory
Level system: 'Level 1' label implies graduated difficulty across the product line
Generous spacing: large cells with plenty of room for developing handwriting
Part of a larger word-work bundle: CVC → Long Vowels → Blends → Digraphs → Trigraphs → Diphthongs

notes: From 'Adapting for Autism' — designed for special education but the multi-sensory approach (see-write-cut-paste) is excellent for any early learner. The cut-and-paste mechanic is a format Homa doesn't have yet. The level system and bundle structure (short a → short e → short i → etc., then long vowels, blends, digraphs) shows a systematic phonics progression. Only the 'short a Level 1' page was visible in the PDF extract — the full product likely contains multiple vowels and levels.
